newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURKISH MINISTER SAYS BUDGET STILL BALANCED IN FEB.
newsitem.headline: TURKISH MINISTER SAYS BUDGET STILL BALANCED IN FEB.

text.p: Turkish Finance Minister Abdullatif Sener said on Monday that the government's plans for a balanced budget in 1997 remained on course in February.
"January turned out to be within the framework of the balanced budget and February is continuing in the same way," Sener told reporters at a news conference.
Turkey's budget showed a deficit of 1,217 trillion lira in 1996. Last December parliament approved the Islamist-led government's balanced budget plan for 1997.
Economists have cast doubt on the plan which programmes in considerable revenues from the country's privatisation plans.
Sener told reporters that the wages of public sector workers were being raised additionally between 18 to 40 percent from January 1, on top of a 30 percent increase for the period announced already.
He also announced plans to introduce a sliding scale wage rise system for public sector workers from July 1, according to which wages will be increased in line with inflation.
Annual wholesale price inflation in Turkey stood at 78.6 percent in February.
The July 1 wage increase will be retroactive for the second quarter and further wage rises will be implemented each quarter, the Finance Minister said.

Public sector workers will also receive an annual increase in line with national economic growth. Turkish gross national product is expected to have grown around seven percent in 1996 and is seen growing some five percent in 1997.
Sener said the additional wage rises effective from January would add a burden of 145 trillion lira to the 1997 budget and would be met by "solid resources" and not through fresh debt issues.
